messages:
lee: Heads-up: customer reported a ~2x provisional charge when a streaming session reconnected after a truncated client retry and then made a toolcall. billing shows two separate provisional rows that later reconciled but customer saw the temporary double charge.

jamal: That pattern rings a bell. We key provisional entries by session_root currently, so when client retries with a new ephemeral session id and the router falls back to a different path we get two protos.

maria: Is the toolcall being attached to the original session_id only? If the fallback path drops the toolcall header we lose linkage.

lee: Trace snippet:```
[2026-03-21T09:42:01Z] session_root=usr-77 start provisional=95 route=router-A
[2026-03-21T09:42:02Z] toolcall=tc-99 attach session=usr-77 charged=30
[2026-03-21T09:42:03Z] reconnect session=usr-77-1 provisional=70 route=router-B
[2026-03-21T09:42:05Z] finalizer: saw charge for tc-99 twice (usr-77 + usr-77-1)
```

natalie: Ugh. Router fallback sometimes re-issues a session id and doesn't copy X-Toolcall-Id or route metadata.

jamal: Proposal 1 (short-term): propagate a stable "routing_epoch" header from ingress -> routers -> finalizer and include routing_epoch in the provisional key. Also, when a toolcall binds, write a backwards pointer from toolcall_id -> provisional_entry(s). Finalizer should dedupe by toolcall_id first.

maria: Proposal 2 (UX): in the console billing lines show a "provisional merge preview" toggle that runs the same dedupe heuristic and shows which prov rows would be merged before finalization. Helpful for support and transparency.

ben: Implementation caveats: increasing pointers/TTL increases kv cardinality. Need to quantify memory/GC impact.

jamal: Agreed. Short-term we can: - keep routing_epoch TTL short (30s) - only keep toolcall pointers for sessions that actually executed tools - sample 10% for hosted to measure cost. For Dedicated we can offer longer windows.

alex: For telemetry add counters: `prov_merge_attempt`, `prov_merge_conflict`, and histogram `prov_merge_latency`. Also emit example traces when conflict rate > 0.1% in a minute.

natalie: Quick header spec:```
X-Routing-Epoch: 2026-03-21T09:42:01Z
X-Toolcall-Id: tc-99
X-Request-Fingerprint: sha256(client-id||prompt-prefix)
```
and provisional key = sha256(session_root||X-Routing-Epoch||maybe-toolcall).

lee: Will the fingerprint break idempotency across clients that intentionally truncate? It should be tolerant: we can include only session_root + toolcall_id when present.

jamal: I'll implement finalizer guard: before creating a finalized charge, check toolcall_id->recent_finalized_charge map for duplicates within window. If found, skip finalize and mark provisional as merged.

maria: Console mock: show merged preview with a small help text: "Merged means the provisional entry was attributed to an existing finalized charge for the same tool invocation; customers are not double billed." Link to support doc.

ops-bot: @channel Incident created: INC-2026-057 (billing-provisional-dup), priority P2. https://rwinternal/incident/INC-2026-057

ben: I'll run a memory/cardinality canary and post numbers. If impact is < 3% we can flip sample to 100% for hosted.

alex: Action items: jamal -> ledger finalizer guard PR (short-term dedupe), natalie -> router header audit & patch, maria -> console prototype + analytics event (prov_preview_click), ben -> canary.

jamal: will open PR tonight targeting canary lane, add feature flag `prov_dedupe_v2`. aiming for small rollout next week.

lee: I'll tell the customer we've identified the root cause and are patching; offer provisional credit for the spike.

maria: Adding support FAQ blurb and the console tooltip copy in a doc.

alex: Thanks everyone. Drop any new variants here (e.g., truncated-prefix + model-swap) so we can cover heuristics.

lee: noted, thanks :thumbsup:
